arml-2000-superrelay-01.title: Base-$b$ expansion
arml-2000-superrelay-01.body:
$Ab^3+Rb^2+Mb+L=2^{10}=1024$ with even digits less than $b$. If $b\ge9$, then $A\ge1$ and $A$ even forces $A\ge2$, $Ab^3\ge2\cdot729>1024$, impossible. If $b=8$: $512A+64R+8M+L=1024$ with $A$ even and nonzero forces $A=2$, $R=M=L=0$ ✓ ($A\ne L$). If $b=7$: the only solution is $2662_7=1024$, but $A=L$. If $b=6$: $4424_6=1024$, but $A=L$. For $b\le5$ the largest value $4444_5=624<1024$. So $b=8$ (and $\sqrt{2000_8}=\sqrt{1024}=2^5$).

**Answer: 8**

arml-2000-superrelay-02.title: Divide
arml-2000-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 1, $8$.)*

If $f$ shares two zeros with $P$, then $f$ divides $P$. Dividing, $P(x)=(x-3)f(x)+(10-5K)x+(3K-6)$ (indeed $(x-3)(x^2+5x+K)=x^3+2x^2+(K-15)x-3K$). The remainder vanishes iff $K=2$.

Check: $(x-3)(x^2+5x+2)=x^3+2x^2-13x-6=x^3+2x^2-(4\cdot2+5)x-6$ ✓.

**Answer: 2**

arml-2000-superrelay-03.title: Diagonal length
arml-2000-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 2, $2$.)*

Let $r=\sqrt2-1$. Each end circle is tangent to two sides at a corner, so its centre is at distance $r\sqrt2$ from the corner; the centres are $2r$ apart. The diagonal is $AC=2\cdot r\sqrt2+2\cdot2r=r(4+2\sqrt2)=(\sqrt2-1)(4+2\sqrt2)=4\sqrt2+4-4-2\sqrt2=2\sqrt2$.

So the side is $2$ and the area is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-2000-superrelay-04.title: Intersect
arml-2000-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 3, $4$.)*

The intersection is $[T-4,2T+10]$, containing $(2T+10)-(T-4)+1=T+15=19$ integers.

**Answer: 19**

arml-2000-superrelay-05.title: Range of sums
arml-2000-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 4, $19$.)*

The smallest sum is $0$ (all zeros) and the largest is $5T$. Starting from all zeros we can raise one chosen element at a time by $1$, so every integer from $0$ to $5T$ occurs. That is $5T+1=96$ sums.

**Answer: 96**

arml-2000-superrelay-06.title: Eliminate $x$
arml-2000-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 5, $96$.)*

$K=-12$. Multiply the first equation by $7$ and the second by $6$ and add: $14y+18y=7K+180$, so $32y=180-84=96$ and $y=3$.

**Answer: 3**

arml-2000-superrelay-07.title: Cases
arml-2000-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 6, $3$.)*

The letters are $A,A,R,R,N,G,E$ (five different letters, with $A$ and $R$ available twice). Three-letter words: all letters different, $5\cdot4\cdot3=60$; a repeated $A$ and one other letter from $\{R,N,G,E\}$: $4\cdot\frac{3!}{2!}=12$; a repeated $R$ and one other letter: $12$. Total $60+12+12=84$.

**Answer: 84**

arml-2000-superrelay-08.title: Four rings
arml-2000-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the Super Relay, position $8$ received $84$ from position $7$ and $12$ from position $9$.)*

Replacing $|x|$ and $|y|$ by $\pm x$, $\pm y$ gives four congruent rings centred at $(\pm2000,\pm2000)$, with inner radius $\sqrt m$ and outer radius $\sqrt M$. They do not overlap (the radii are tiny compared with $2000$). Each ring has area $\pi M-\pi m$, so the total is $4\pi(84-12)=288\pi$.

**Answer: $288\pi$**

arml-2000-superrelay-09.title: 3-4-5 triangles
arml-2000-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 10, $\frac35$.)*

$K=54$. Let $AB=x$. The legs are $5x$ and the bases $x$ and $7x$, so each leg overhangs by $\frac{7x-x}2=3x$ horizontally; the height is $\sqrt{(5x)^2-(3x)^2}=4x$. The perimeter is $x+7x+5x+5x=18x=54$, so $x=3$ and the height is $12$.

**Answer: 12**

arml-2000-superrelay-10.title: Supplementary angles
arml-2000-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 11, $\frac{13}4$.)*

$K=3$, $\cos B=\frac{8}{10}=\frac45$. Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary, so $\sin A=\sin B=\frac35$ (in general $\sin B=\frac{2K}{K^2+1}$).

**Answer: $\frac35$**

arml-2000-superrelay-11.title: Slope condition
arml-2000-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 12, $66$.)*

$K=-3$. Slope of $AB$: $\frac{-3-2}{5-1}=-\frac54$; slope of $AC$: $\frac{7-2}{-3-1}=-\frac54$ ✓. The line is $y-2=-\frac54(x-1)$, i.e. $y=-\frac54x+\frac{13}4$, so the $y$-intercept is $\frac{13}4$. (In general collinearity gives $K^2-3K-18=0$, $K=-3$ or $6$; $T=66$ selects $K=-3$.)

**Answer: $\frac{13}4$**

arml-2000-superrelay-12.title: Factor
arml-2000-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 13, $20$.)*

$2000^T=(2\cdot10^3)^T=2^T\cdot10^{3T}$, so $x=3T=60$ and $y$ is the last digit of $2^{20}=1048576$, namely $6$. So $x+y=66$.

**Answer: 66**

arml-2000-superrelay-13.title: Isosceles pieces
arml-2000-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 14, $2$.)*

$PDAE$ is a parallelogram. $\triangle BDP\sim\triangle BAC$ is isosceles, so $DP=DB$ and $AD+DP=AD+DB=AB$. Likewise $AE+EP=AC$. So the perimeter is $AB+AC=20$, independent of $T$ and $P$.

**Answer: 20**
